questions.stem_en: An account has 300 EC2 instances in one Region. All instances use IMDSv2 and run SSM Agent 3.2.582.0 or later, but many of them have no IAM instance profile, so they do not appear as Systems Manager managed nodes. The company wants all current and future instances in the Region to become managed nodes without creating or attaching instance profiles. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Create an instance profile with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy, and attach it to every instance that lacks one.
Turn on Default Host Management Configuration in the Region, and use the default role that it provides.
Add an inbound rule for HTTPS on port 443 to each instance's security group so that Systems Manager can connect to SSM Agent.
Turn on Default Host Management Configuration, and switch the instances to IMDSv1 so that they can get the role's credentials.

explanation.summary: Default Host Management Configuration を有効にすると、インスタンスプロファイルを手作業で作らなくても、そのアカウントとリージョンで IMDSv2 を使い SSM Agent 3.2.582.0 以降を入れたすべてのインスタンスが自動でマネージドインスタンスになります。既定のロールは、Systems Manager で管理するのに必要な最小の権限を持ちます。

per_choice.A: マネージドノードにはなりますが、インスタンスプロファイルを作ってアタッチしないという要件に反し、今後のインスタンスにも作業が要ります。
per_choice.B: 正しい。条件を満たす今と今後のインスタンスが、インスタンスプロファイル無しで自動で管理されます。
per_choice.C: SSM Agent が Systems Manager への接続をすべて始めるので、受信のルールは要らず、権限の問題も解決しません。
per_choice.D: Default Host Management Configuration は IMDSv1 に対応しておらず、IMDSv2 が必要です。

references.quote: Using Default Host Management Configuration, you can manage EC2 instances without having to manually create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) instance profile.
all instances using Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) in the AWS Region and AWS account with SSM Agent version 3.2.582.0 or later installed automatically become managed instances.
Default Host Management Configuration doesn't support Instance Metadata Service Version 1.
you don't need to configure your firewall to allow inbound traffic to your instances for Systems Manager.

questions.stem_en: EC2 instances in private subnets have SSM Agent and the required IAM permissions, but they do not appear as Systems Manager managed nodes. The subnets have no route to the internet, and the security team will not allow outbound internet access. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take so that the instances can be managed by Systems Manager? (Choose TWO.)

choices_en.text: Create VPC endpoints for the ssm, ssmmessages, and ec2messages services in the VPC.
Allow outbound HTTPS traffic on port 443 from the instances to the VPC endpoints.
Add an inbound rule for port 443 from Systems Manager to the instances' security group.
Add a NAT gateway and a route to the internet so that SSM Agent can reach the public endpoints.
Install the CloudWatch agent on the instances so that they report their status to Systems Manager.

explanation.summary: SSM Agent は Systems Manager のサービスへの接続をすべて自分から始め、ssm・ssmmessages・ec2messages のエンドポイントと HTTPS（443 番ポート）で通信します。インターネットへの外向きのアクセスを使わない時は、VPC エンドポイントを使います。

per_choice.A: 正しい。インターネットに出ずに、SSM Agent が通信するエンドポイントへ VPC の中から届きます。
per_choice.B: 正しい。SSM Agent は HTTPS の 443 番ポートで外向きに接続するので、エンドポイントへの外向きの通信を許します。
per_choice.C: SSM Agent が接続を始めるので、受信の通信を許す必要はありません。
per_choice.D: 動きますが、外向きのインターネットのアクセスを許さないという要件に反します。
per_choice.E: 状態を Systems Manager へ送るのは SSM Agent で、CloudWatch エージェントは関係ありません。

references.quote: The alternative to using a VPC endpoint is to allow outbound internet access on your managed instances.
the managed instances must also allow HTTPS (port 443) outbound traffic to the following endpoints: ssm.region.amazonaws.com, ssmmessages.region.amazonaws.com, ec2messages.region.amazonaws.com.
SSM Agent initiates all connections to the Systems Manager service in the cloud.
SSM Agent then sends status and execution information back to the Systems Manager service by using the Amazon Message Gateway Service (ssmmessages).
